title: Vector Databases: From Zero to RAG
tagline: A complete, hands-on course that takes you from "what is a vector?" to building and evaluating a production-grade Retrieval-Augmented Generation system.
overview: This course provides an in-depth understanding of modern vector databases, high-dimensional semantic search, and production-grade Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. Students learn how to navigate the shift from traditional lexical/keyword search (BM25, TF-IDF) to embedding-driven semantic search, exploring both theoretical foundations and hands-on implementations. The curriculum covers mathematical similarity metrics, Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) algorithms (HNSW, IVF, PQ), chunking strategies, and benchmarking leading vector databases (ChromaDB, FAISS, Qdrant, pgvector). In the capstone module, students build a full-stack RAG pipeline with ChromaDB and open-weight LLMs (Qwen 2.5), quantitatively evaluate retrieval quality using Recall@k and MRR, and harden the system with cross-encoder reranking and hybrid search.
learningObjectives: Understand why traditional keyword search breaks down and how semantic vector representations resolve lexical mismatches.
Master text and multimodal embeddings, vector spaces, and dimensional reduction techniques like PCA and t-SNE.
Implement and analyze mathematical similarity metrics: Cosine Similarity, Dot Product, and Euclidean (L2) distance.
Demystify Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) indexing structures including HNSW, IVF, Product Quantization (PQ), and LSH.
Architecturally compare and benchmark FAISS, Qdrant, pgvector, ChromaDB, Weaviate, Milvus, and Pinecone.
Design and tune production text-chunking strategies (fixed-size, sentence-aware, recursive) and measure their impact on retrieval.
Develop production workflows in ChromaDB from collection indexing to advanced metadata filtering and persistence.
Construct an end-to-end RAG pipeline (Retrieve, Augment, Generate) using ChromaDB and open-weight models (Qwen 2.5) with zero paid API costs.
Rigorously evaluate retrieval quality using Recall@k and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), hardening pipelines with Cross-Encoder reranking.

keyTopics.title: Keyword vs Semantic Search
keyTopics.desc: Lexical limitations, synonyms, context ambiguity, and dense embedding spaces.

keyTopics.title: Embeddings & Vector Geometry
keyTopics.desc: Tokenization, transformer embeddings, dense representations, and dimensional visualization.

keyTopics.title: Similarity Metrics from Scratch
keyTopics.desc: Cosine similarity, dot product, and Euclidean distance formulas implemented in NumPy.

keyTopics.title: ANN Algorithms Under the Hood
keyTopics.desc: Graph-based (HNSW), inverted file (IVF), and quantization (PQ) indexing for rapid nearest neighbor search.

keyTopics.title: Vector Database Landscape
keyTopics.desc: Architectural tradeoffs between embedded libraries (FAISS), dedicated engines (ChromaDB, Qdrant), and SQL extensions (pgvector).

keyTopics.title: Document Chunking Strategies
keyTopics.desc: Fixed vs recursive vs semantic chunking, boundary detection, token preservation, and PDF preprocessing.

keyTopics.title: ChromaDB Core Architecture
keyTopics.desc: Collections, document ingestion, embeddings functions, metadata filtering, and persistent vector storage.

keyTopics.title: Production RAG Pipeline
keyTopics.desc: The complete Retrieve-Augment-Generate loop paired with open-weight models (Qwen 2.5).

keyTopics.title: Evaluation, Reranking & Hardening
keyTopics.desc: Precision benchmarking via Recall@k and MRR, cross-encoder reranking, and hybrid search.

parts.title: Part 1 — Fundamentals
parts.description: Establish the foundational shift from keyword search to semantic search, understand high-dimensional embeddings, and implement similarity metrics from scratch.

parts.title: Part 2 — How a Vector Database Works Under the Hood
parts.description: Deep-dive into indexing algorithms that enable search across millions of vectors, compare the vector database ecosystem, and engineer document chunking pipelines.

parts.title: Part 3 — ChromaDB and RAG
parts.description: Build production vector collections with ChromaDB, orchestrate an end-to-end RAG architecture with open-weight models, and evaluate performance with quantitative metrics and reranking.

sessions.topic: Introduction and the Problem with Traditional Search
sessions.description: Why traditional keyword search breaks down and how semantic vector representations solve the lexical gap.
How text and images become dense numerical vectors, exploring embedding spaces and dimensionality visualization.
The math behind geometric similarity: cosine similarity, dot product, and Euclidean distance built from scratch in NumPy.
Approximate Nearest Neighbor indexing structures (HNSW, IVF, PQ, LSH) that enable sub-linear search latency.
Comprehensive architectural benchmark comparing FAISS, ChromaDB, Qdrant, and pgvector for different workloads.
Text chunking strategies (fixed, recursive, semantic) and their quantitative impact on retrieval quality across real PDFs.
Installing and configuring ChromaDB collections, running complex queries, metadata filtering, and persistent stores.
Constructing an end-to-end RAG system: retrieving relevant chunks, augmenting system prompts, and generating answers with Qwen 2.5.
Evaluating retrieval with Recall@k and MRR metrics, hardening against hallucinations, and boosting precision via Cross-Encoder reranking.

whoThisCourseIsFor: Backend & Software Engineers building semantic search engines, contextual recommendation systems, or enterprise knowledge bases.
Data Scientists & Machine Learning Engineers designing, testing, and evaluating production RAG architectures.
System Architects evaluating vector database solutions (FAISS, ChromaDB, Qdrant, pgvector) for their tech stack.
Students & Practitioners seeking a structured, project-driven, and mathematically sound path into vector search.
prerequisites: Basic Python proficiency (functions, loops, lists, dictionaries, imports).
Familiarity with the command line and Jupyter notebooks / Google Colab.
A free Google account for accessing and executing Colab notebooks.
No prior experience with vector databases, embeddings, or deep learning required.
